SwiftPaxos: Fast Geo-Replicated State Machines
==========
<!-- [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos) -->

This repository contains the prototype implementation of SwiftPaxos, a new state-machine replication protocol for geo-distributed systems.
SwiftPaxos is a _faster Paxos without compromises_.
In the best case, it executes a state-machine command in two message delays (one round-trip), and three otherwise.
SwiftPaxos was [presented](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) at the 21st USENIX Symposium on Networked Systems Design and Implementation ([NSDI '24](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24)).

Installation
------------

    git clone https://github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos.git
    cd swiftpaxos
    go install github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos

Implemented protocols
---------------------

|  Protocol               | Comments                                          |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| SwiftPaxos              | See our NSDI'24 [paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) for the full details.|
| Paxos                   | The classic Paxos protocol.                       |
| N<sup>2</sup>Paxos      | All-to-all variant of Paxos.                      |
| CURP                    | CURP implemented over N<sup>2</sup>Paxos.         |
| Fast Paxos              | Fast Paxos with uncoordinated collision recovery. |
| EPaxos                  | A [corrected][epaxos_correct] version of EPaxos.  |

This software is based on the [Egalitarian Paxos](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos) code base, as well as the corrections made [here](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos).

Usage
-----
#### participants
There are three types of participants: *master*, *servers* and *clients*. 
The servers and clients implement the protocol logic. 
The master maintains the configuration of the system.

#### deployment configuration
To setup a run, the participants read deployment configuration file. 
See [aws.conf][config] for an example of configuration file for AWS EC2.

#### launching a participant

Master:
    
    swiftpaxos -run master -config conf.conf

Server:

    swiftpaxos -run server -config conf.conf -alias server_name

Client:

    swiftpaxos -run client -config conf.conf -alias client_name

#### command line options

    -alias alias
        An alias of this participant
    -config file
        Deployment config file (required)
    -latency file
        Latency config file
    -log file
        Path to the log file
    -protocol protocol
        Protocol to run. Overwrites protocol field of the config file
    -quorum file
        Quorum config file
    -run participant
        Run a participant

See [quorum.conf][quorum] and [latency.conf][latency] for an example of quorum and latency configuration files.

Flint
-----

To have an idea on how different replication protocols would compare, we wrote a tool named [Flint][flint]. 
Flint takes as input a set of AWS regions.
It computes the expected latencies and estimates how the protocols perform in such a deployment.

[epaxos_correct]: https://github.com/otrack/on-epaxos-correctness

		rep := swift.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,

		curp.MaxDescRoutines = 100
		rep := curp.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,

		rpc.Register(rep)

		rep := fastpaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, f, c, logger)

	case "n2paxos":

		log.Println("Starting Paxos replica...")

	case "epaxos":

		rep := epaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, false, false, 0, false, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)

	rpc.HandleHTTP()

var (

	logFile      = flag.String("log", "", "Path to the log `file`")
	machineAlias = flag.String("alias", "", "An `alias` of this participant")
	machineType  = flag.String("run", "server", "Run a `participant`, which is either a server (or replica), a client or a master")
	protocol     = flag.String("protocol", "", "Protocol to run. Overwrites `protocol` field of the config file")
	quorum       = flag.String("quorum", "", "Quorum config `file`")
)

func main() {
	flag.Parse()

	if *confs == "" {
		flag.Usage()
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	c, err := config.Read(*confs, *machineAlias)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println(err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if *protocol != "" {
		c.Protocol = *protocol
	}
	defs.LatencyConf = *latency

	switch *machineType {
	case "replica":
		fallthrough
	case "server":
		c.MachineType = config.ReplicaMachine
	case "client":
		c.MachineType = config.ClientMachine
	case "master":
		c.MachineType = config.MasterMachine
	default:
		fmt.Println("Unknown participant type")
		flag.Usage()
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	c.Quorum = *quorum

	run(c)
}

func run(c *config.Config) {
	switch c.MachineType {
	case config.MasterMachine:
		runMaster(c)
	case config.ClientMachine:
		runClient(c, true)
	case config.ReplicaMachine:
		runReplica(c, dlog.New(*logFile, true))
	}
}

func runMaster(c *config.Config) {
	m := master.New(len(c.ReplicaAddrs), c.MasterPort, c, dlog.New(*logFile, true))
	m.Run()
}

func runClient(c *config.Config, verbose bool) {
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < c.Clones+1; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func(i int) {
			runSingleClient(c, i, verbose)
			wg.Done()
		}(i)
	}
	wg.Wait()
}

	var l *dlog.Logger

## F1. Recovery masks remote values with a local NONE reply at the new ballot

**Expected.**  A recovery leader that has no value for an instance must include
its own empty vote without claiming a value ballot.  The other replies, which
may report an `ACCEPTED` or `COMMITTED` value at a real value ballot, must win
the `VBallot` comparison in `handlePrepareReply` (`epaxos.go:1239-1246`).  This
is the recovery invariant encoded by the saved `lb.ballot = inst.vbal` at
`epaxos.go:1145` and by the "only replies from the highest ballot are taken
into account" comment at `1229`.

**Affected code.**  `startRecoveryForInstance`, `epaxos.go:1153-1161`:

```go
inst.bal = lb.lastTriedBallot
inst.vbal = lb.lastTriedBallot       // old value ballot is discarded
preply := &PrepareReply{
    r.Id, replica, instance,
    inst.bal, inst.vbal,             // VBallot is now the new prepare ballot
    inst.Status, inst.Cmds, inst.Seq, inst.Deps}
```

When the local instance is `NONE`, `inst.Cmds` is nil and `inst.Status` is
`NONE`, but the synthetic reply claims `VBallot == lastTriedBallot`.  In
`handlePrepareReply` the local reply is the first element of
`prepareReplies`; `element.VBallot >= lb.ballot` is therefore true, and it
installs `lb.cmds = nil`, `lb.status = NONE`, and `lb.ballot = lastTriedBallot`.
Every remote reply at a lower value ballot is then ignored.  The resulting
sub-case is 6, so `startPhase1` is called with `state.NOOP()`.

**Necessary conditions.**  `executeCommands` has queued
`instancesToRecover` for an instance this replica does not have (or has only a
lower-ballot value), and a slow quorum of prepare replies reports a committed
or accepted command.  The replica need not be the instance owner; recovery is
started by the execution timeout for any row.

**Observed.**  `TestAuditRecoveryDoesNotDiscardCommittedRemoteValue` starts
recovery for instance 2.0 with no local copy, then delivers two replies for
that instance with `Status: COMMITTED`, `VBallot: 7`, and a PUT command.  The
recovering replica instead starts phase 1 with NOOP:

```
recovery discarded the committed command: Status=1 Cmds=[{0 0 []}] (phase-1 result)
```

`TestAuditRecoveryLocalReplyKeepsValueBallot` shows the local reply itself:

```
old bal=5 old vbal=2 new lastTriedBallot=5 local reply Ballot=5 VBallot=5 Status=3
```

The local reply reports `VBallot=5` although the stored value was at `vbal=2`.

**Impact.**  A committed client command can be replaced by NOOP when any
replica without that command enters recovery.  This is an agreement/safety
violation, independent of the codec defect in F2.

## F2. `PrepareReply` does not serialize `VBallot`

**Expected.**  `PrepareReply` has a `VBallot int32` field (`epaxos/defs.go:20-28`)
and `handlePrepareReply` relies on it to choose the newest value
(`epaxos.go:1239-1246`, `1261`).  A wire round trip must preserve every field.
The sibling messages `PreAcceptReply` and `TryPreAcceptReply` both encode their
`VBallot` fields (`defs.go:841`, `1181`).

**Affected code.**  `PrepareReply.Marshal` (`defs.go:153-208`) uses a 17-byte
fixed header containing `AcceptorId`, `Replica`, `Instance`, `Ballot`, and
`Status`; it never writes `VBallot`.  `PrepareReply.Unmarshal`
(`defs.go:210-253`) never reads it.  The header is 4+4+4+4+1 bytes, matching a
struct without `VBallot`.

**Necessary conditions.**  Any prepare reply that travels between replicas and
reports a nonzero value ballot.  Recovery is the only path that sends
`PrepareReply`.

```

out=... VBallot:0 ...

recovery selected [{1 1 [115 116 97 108 101]}] (Status=1)
```

value is selected, so a stale pre-accepted value can overwrite an accepted

## F11. Prepare-reply robustness and retry omissions (source-based)

At `epaxos.go:1205-1206`, `inst.lb` is read before the `inst == nil` check at
`1212`, so an unexpected prepare reply for an instance not present locally
panics.  The normal sender only prepares instances it knows, so this is a
robustness issue unless messages are duplicated or state is reset.

returns, but unlike `handlePreAcceptReply` and `paxos.handlePrepareReply`,
there is no `if nacks+1 > N/2 { makeBallot; bcastPrepare }`.  A recovery whose
responders have all moved to a higher ballot can therefore keep waiting
without retrying at a higher ballot.  This is a liveness issue; I did not
produce a scheduler that shows the stall end to end.
